title: Long-form reading spine
guidance: Keep the reading measure stable across the article
Externalize article orientation with clear headings and local navigation
Give tables citations and notes explicit narrow-screen behavior
avoid: Decorative sidebars that compete with reading

title: Evidence-first decision trail
guidance: State the specific promise before asking for commitment
Place real evidence at the point where doubt naturally appears
Match CTA language to the commitment distance
avoid: A primary CTA before purpose is understandable

title: Task workbench
guidance: Keep frequent controls visible
Group by task and state rather than organizational ownership
Preserve expert density while clarifying hierarchy
avoid: Hiding expert controls to satisfy generic simplicity advice
Marketing-page card rhythm inside the tool

title: Source-visible trust hub
guidance: Expose scope boundaries near the claims they qualify
Make evidence tests changelog and method logic navigable
Use transparency as structure rather than a trust badge

title: Bounded guided flow
guidance: Keep current state and exit visible
Make stop conditions more prominent as risk rises
End with a small explicit completion state
avoid: Progress pressure that overrides user hesitation

title: Artifact-led experience
guidance: Let the work dominate the first meaningful view
Keep orientation controls quiet but persistent
Use motion only when it clarifies sequence or material
avoid: Interface decoration that competes with the work

title: Reference library
guidance: Support browse and exact retrieval separately
Keep taxonomy visible enough to build a mental map
Preserve dense option sets for expert readers
avoid: Replacing a real taxonomy with a small marketing menu
Search as the only orientation mechanism

title: Editorial letter close
guidance: Close in the established author voice
Explain what the reader receives and what support enables
Keep the subscription action distinct from article conclusions
avoid: Interrupting the argument with repeated modal asks
